task_setup.incentive_check: at vx=0.03, ideal tracking under w_vel=10 gives +0.3/step advantage over standing (0 tracking error vs 0.03 error * 10), before movement penalties -- confirmed as a real, if modest, per-step incentive; NOT treated as proof that stepping would be discovered.

training_outcome: All 3 seeds preserved standing throughout (fall_rate stayed near 0.0 for the full 400k-step budget in every seed, consistent with U27-U29's own standing-preservation result). No training-time signal of destabilization requiring an early stop.

measurements: foot clearance / alternating touchdown / stance-foot slip
evaluation.zero_command_all_seeds: 200/200 steps, no fall, near-zero forward drift (0.011-0.041m over 4s) -- standing retained in every seed, as expected.

seed1.note: forward progress WITHOUT any genuine (>=60ms) foot-airborne phase -- weight-shifting/sliding, not stepping

evaluation.foot_clearance_context: 1-3mm in every seed, every condition -- noise-level vibration, not a real swing-phase lift. Zero genuine swing phases (>=3 consecutive control steps airborne) on EITHER foot, in ANY of the 6 seed x condition combinations.
evaluation.torque_and_tracking: actuator saturation mean 27.5-36.0%, joint tracking error mean 0.008-0.010 rad across all conditions -- unremarkable, well within modeled authority. Movement (what little occurred) was not actuator-constrained.
evaluation.milestone_check: The first walking milestone (several genuine alternating steps with sustained forward progress while upright) is NOT MET, in any of the 3 seeds. Reported plainly, per instruction NOT automatically classified as a balance failure -- standing was retained cleanly in every case; this is a 'stayed standing' outcome, not a fall or instability outcome.

exploration_and_cost_of_moving_check.instruction: if the policy stays standing, inspect exploration and the cost of moving -- do not just report 'balance failure'

measured_final_exploration_std.units: normalized action-space units, all 12 joints similar

exploration_and_cost_of_moving_check.context: roughly HALF of U27's already-conservative starting std (0.0498 at init_logstd=-3.0), having decayed further through U28's and U29's recovery training, which reinforced smooth/quiet corrections (U26 raised w_action_rate specifically to suppress jitter). At hip_pitch's own offset_scale (0.42 rad), 0.029 normalized-std translates to ~0.012 rad (~0.7 degree) of 1-sigma per-step swing -- far too small for PPO's on-policy sampling to ever produce a clean, deliberate leg lift, regardless of whether the reward would pay for one if sampled.
exploration_and_cost_of_moving_check.conclusion: The most likely explanation is exploration magnitude, not reward sign or actuator limits: the policy lineage's exploration was deliberately, successfully suppressed across U27-U29 specifically to preserve standing, and that same suppression now appears to be preventing it from ever sampling the kind of large, coordinated leg motion that stepping requires. The +0.3/step tracking incentive exists but cannot be discovered if it is never sampled.
exploration_and_cost_of_moving_check.not_yet_checked: action-rate/effort penalty magnitude at a hypothetical stepping gait's actual jitter level (would need a scripted-gait probe, similar to U25's actuator-response tests, to measure the REAL cost of a stepping-scale motion against the achievable +0.3/step benefit) -- flagged, not done this session.

net_assessment: Standing was retained cleanly in all 3 seeds under both zero and 0.03 m/s commands -- the reward/observation infrastructure fixes (upright sign, command normalization) did their job without destabilizing anything. But no seed discovered genuine stepping; one showed sliding-without-stepping, the other two stayed essentially static regardless of command. The leading, evidence-supported explanation is that exploration std has decayed too far (through three prior training generations optimized specifically for quiet standing/recovery) to ever sample the motion a stepping gait requires -- not a reward-incentive problem (the +0.3/step advantage is real and unchanged) and not an actuator-authority problem (saturation and tracking are unremarkable). This points toward either a deliberate, bounded exploration boost targeted at the walking task specifically, or a fresh initialization strategy for locomotion analogous to U27's for standing -- flagged for the next decision, not started here.
